title: LaTER: Efficient Test-Time Reasoning via Latent Exploration and Explicit Verification
data_curation: LaTER introduces LATENT-SWITCH-69K, a 69,745-example supervised corpus built from reasoning traces sampled from Dolci-Think-SFT-32B and distilled by a stronger reasoning teacher. For each source problem the teacher first produces a short solution intuition (a few-sentence high-level plan, no full derivation), then a shorter explicit CoT conditioned on the problem plus that intuition; each retained record holds problem, intuition, compressed CoT, and final answer. The distilled-CoT compression ratio is mean 0.612 / median 0.569 (kept ~57-61% of original length). Difficulty split: easy 9.5%, medium 65.5%, hard 25.0%; domain mix is math ~37%, code ~34%, science ~5%, remainder instruction-following/general knowledge. Per-example latent budget is tied to intuition length (~L/2 steps), giving mean 41.49 / median 40.00 latent steps, normalized to the 40-50-step range found optimal in training-free experiments. Curriculum metadata groups by difficulty so early training can emphasize easier examples.
curriculum: Training is a single fine-tuning stage rather than a multi-stage RL pipeline; the paper's 'two-stage' notion is the inference-time latent-then-explicit paradigm, not a training-stage ordering. The supervised objective combines token-level cross-entropy (split into a CoT term with lambda_CoT=0.5 and a non-CoT term), cached top-k teacher self-distillation KL (lambda_KL=0.25, T=1.0), and a gated latent-halting loss (base weight 0.025, dynamically gated by the CE moving average). The corpus carries difficulty metadata letting early training emphasize easier (then medium/hard) examples, but no explicit warmup/anneal schedule across separate stages is described. Evaluation compares four systems on the same benchmarks: standard CoT, CoT-SFT (same data/objectives minus the latent component), training-free LaTER, and trained LaTER, framing the contribution as a single-stage architecture-plus-data intervention rather than a curriculum.
method: LaTER (Latent-Then-Explicit Reasoning) is a hybrid test-time paradigm: a bounded continuous latent rollout for exploration, then explicit CoT for verification, reusing the latent KV cache so explicit decoding conditions on the latent trajectory. Training-free: the final-layer hidden state h_s is mapped to input-embedding space via pseudo-inverse W_out^+ W_in (the LatentMAS construction) and fed back without token commitment; switching uses the adaptive rule switch(s)=1[H_s>tau_H or y_hat_s in T_stop] (entropy threshold tau_H=7 and terminating-token probes like <|im_end|>). Trained LaTER replaces the pseudo-inverse with a learned projector g_phi, adds <latent_think>/</latent_think> boundary tokens, and supervises latent placeholders only indirectly via gradients from downstream explicit/answer tokens (no CE inside the latent segment). Loss L=L_CE+lambda_KL*L_KL+L_halt^eff: CE split into CoT (lambda_CoT=0.5) and non-CoT terms; top-k (k=128) teacher KL self-distillation (T=1.0, lambda_KL=0.25); a halting loss penalizing forbidden structural tokens plus BCE at the boundary, gated by EMA(L_CE)/L_CE (base weight 0.025). Optimized with AdamW (lr 1e-7), DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 on 8xA800 80G (~5 days).
eval_metrics: Evaluates accuracy and total token usage (latent steps + emitted explicit tokens) on AIME 2025 (via MathArena), MATH-500, GSM8K, GPQA, ARC-Challenge, HumanEval+, and MBPP+. Backbones: Qwen3-14B (main, trained base), DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, OLMo3-32B-Think, with Qwen3 decoding config (temp 0.6, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, max_new_tokens 38192). Training-free LaTER on Qwen3-14B: AIME 2025 73.3% (+3.3) at 10,661 tokens (-32% vs 15,730), MATH-500 97.2% (+3.8) at 2,887 tokens (-17%), GSM8K 93.2% (-26% tokens), ARC 96.5%, with consistent token cuts across all three backbones. Trained LaTER (Qwen3-14B) gets best accuracy on most and lowest tokens on all seven benchmarks: AIME 2025 80.0% (+10.0) at 10,575 (-33%), MATH-500 96.4% (+3.0), GSM8K 94.8%, ARC 96.7%, GPQA 63.1%, HumanEval+ 92.2%, MBPP+ 82.8%. CoT-SFT (same data, no latent) reaches AIME 73.3% at 12,687 tokens, isolating the latent architecture's added efficiency.
key_results: Trained LaTER on Qwen3-14B reaches 80.0% on AIME 2025 (+10.0 over the CoT baseline's 70.0%) while using 33% fewer tokens (10,575 vs 15,730), with best/lowest-token results across 7 benchmarks (MATH-500 96.4%, HumanEval+ 92.2%). Training-free LaTER on Qwen3-14B lifts AIME 2025 70.0%->73.3% and MATH-500 93.4%->97.2% with 32%/17% token cuts. CoT-SFT matches AIME 73.3% but at 12,687 tokens, showing the latent-first design beats mere trace shortening.
evolution_note: LaTER builds on the 2025-26 latent-reasoning line (Coconut, SoftCoT, Latent-SFT, CoLaR) and training-free variants (Soft Thinking, SeLaR, LatentMAS), reacting against fully replacing explicit CoT-which degrades symbolic tasks like MATH-500/AIME-by splitting labor: latent exploration for search, explicit CoT for verification. In 2026 it motivates learned instance-adaptive halting policies and extension of latent-then-explicit reasoning to longer open-ended and multimodal settings.
